newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFIs sell firm to German MEWA Metallwaren.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFIs sell firm to German MEWA Metallwaren.

text.p: National Investment Fund (NFI) Progress (No. 4) in Poland's mass privatisation scheme has sold its FAM SA metals firm to Germany's MEWA Metallwaren Naumburg GmbH for 4.6 million zlotys, the fund said on Thursday.

"On the power of the signed contract the investor will take 60 percent of the firm's shares, with 33 percent (of the firm) having belonged to NFI Progress and 27 percent to the remaining funds," NFI Progress said in a statement.
The deal, which sees new machinery installed at FAM, must be approved by the anti-monopoly office and interior minstry.

Progress said it would use its proceeds to raise the capital in other firms in its portfolio: fruit and vegetable processor Tymbark, furniture maker Fameg and manufacturer of automotive lighting accessories Zelmot.

FAM, whose full name is Fabryki Akcesoriow Meblowych and which specialises in producing metal parts for furniture, hinges and door handles, made a net profit of 1.5 million zlotys last year on sales of 36.8 million.
